findings.highlight: Listening to it now, the fact that this was a message from ten days ago is quite hard to believe. Things in life can be so surreal sometimes.
findings.evidenceJa:
今聞くと、
これがたった十日ほど前のことというのが、
信じ難くもあり、無常でもある。
findings.explanation: 無常 marks the painful impermanence of events only ten days old; the English calls life surreal.
findings.japanese:
今聞くと、
これがたった十日ほど前のことというのが、
信じ難くもあり、無常でもある。
findings.todokanai: Listening to it now, the fact that this was a message from ten days ago is quite hard to believe. Things in life can be so surreal sometimes.

findings.evidenceJa: それから朝まで、依緒と武也からのコールが一時間おきくらいに数件続いてる。
findings.explanation: Io and Takeya leave several more calls at intervals of roughly one hour until morning. The English says they call several times per hour, multiplying the frequency and materially changing the chronology of Haruki's unanswered messages.
findings.japanese:
それから朝まで、依緒と武也からのコールが
一時間おきくらいに数件続いてる。
findings.todokanai: Afterward, Io and Takeya continue to call me several times an hour until the next morning.

findings.highlight: "There's nothing I can do but trust her… She doesn't joke around when it comes to the stage."
findings.evidenceJa:
「信じるしかないだろ…
舞台には嘘はつかないよ、あいつは」
findings.explanation: Chiaki never lies to the stage, an artistic-truth claim paired with the next line's claim that she lies everywhere else; the English says only that she does not joke around about the stage.
findings.japanese:
「信じるしかないだろ…
舞台には嘘はつかないよ、あいつは」
findings.todokanai: "There's nothing I can do but trust her… She doesn't joke around when it comes to the stage."

findings.evidenceJa: 一枚だけＲメディアってところがまた…
findings.explanation: Takeya finds it suspicious that this is the only recordable R-format disc among Haruki's media. The English mistakes Rメディア for an age rating and calls it an R-rated disc, breaking the clue that a lone home-recorded DVD may contain something private.
findings.japanese:
「お！　怪しいＤＶＤ発見！
一枚だけＲメディアってところがまた…」
findings.todokanai: "Oh! Here's a suspicious DVD! Still, you only got one R-rated disc, huh…"

findings.highlight: he seems to have figured me out
findings.evidenceJa: なんて計算する俺に少しの嫌悪感。
findings.explanation: Haruki feels a measure of disgust toward himself for calculating that his thorough cleaning would protect him from Takeya's trap. The English instead says he is uncomfortable because Takeya has figured him out, moving the judgment outside Haruki and erasing his self-condemnation.
findings.japanese: …なんて計算する俺に少しの嫌悪感。
findings.todokanai: …Though I do feel a little uncomfortable about the fact that he seems to have figured me out.

findings.highlight: The fact that I'm still hung up on Kazusa. And that Setsuna still can't get over how I feel about Kazusa.
findings.evidenceJa:
俺がまだ、かずさのことを引きずっていることも、
雪菜がまだ、かずさと俺のことを引きずっていることも。
findings.explanation: Setsuna remains hung up on Kazusa and Haruki as a pair or history; the English narrows this to how Haruki feels about Kazusa.
findings.japanese:
俺がまだ、かずさのことを引きずっていることも、
雪菜がまだ、かずさと俺のことを引きずっていることも。
findings.todokanai: The fact that I'm still hung up on Kazusa. And that Setsuna still can't get over how I feel about Kazusa.

findings.highlight: I've always thought that there's no need for her to force herself any longer
findings.evidenceJa: ずっと『頑張るのをやめたい』って、思ってたんだから。
findings.explanation: Setsuna herself had long wanted to stop trying so hard, which explains why acknowledging Haruki's wrongdoing would destroy the equilibrium she had forced herself to maintain. The English turns that desire into Haruki's opinion that she need not try, changing whose exhaustion and will drive the impasse.
findings.japanese: ずっと『頑張るのをやめたい』って、思ってたんだから。
findings.todokanai: I've always thought that there's no need for her to force herself any longer.

findings.highlight: had I known that I would be able to settle things with Setsuna simply by coming clean to them
findings.evidenceJa: もしも話が、雪菜との事だけで終わってたなら、こんな、数年来の友人にまで不興を買うような事実、本当に俺は喋ってたんだろうか？
findings.explanation: Haruki asks whether, if the discussion had ended with the Setsuna problem alone, he truly would have volunteered the further fact that would earn even his longtime friends' disgust. The English invents a belief that confessing to them could settle matters with Setsuna, replacing his admission that Io's discovery may be the only reason the second betrayal came out.
findings.japanese:
もしも話が、雪菜との事だけで終わってたなら、
こんな、数年来の友人にまで不興を買うような事実、
本当に俺は喋ってたんだろうか？
findings.todokanai: Would I have been able to bring myself to divulge such a disheartening truth to these long-standing friends of mine, had I known that I would be able to settle things with Setsuna simply by coming clean to them?

findings.highlight: "Getting into a casual relationship, messing around and acting on a whim… You don't do those kinds of things, Haruki! So then why…!?"
findings.evidenceJa:
「行きずりだって遊びだって気まぐれだって、
春希絶対に引きずるじゃない！
なのに、なんで…っ」
findings.explanation: Io says that even a passing encounter, mere play, or whim would inevitably stay with Haruki; the English says he does not do those things.
findings.japanese:
「行きずりだって遊びだって気まぐれだって、
春希絶対に引きずるじゃない！
なのに、なんで…っ」
findings.todokanai: "Getting into a casual relationship, messing around and acting on a whim… You don't do those kinds of things, Haruki! So then why…!?"

findings.highlight: she's someone I consider a friend
findings.evidenceJa: 一部を除いて、友達と認めた相手には、限りないお節介を焼く、俺の類友。
findings.explanation: Haruki calls Io his kindred spirit: with the stated exception, once she accepts someone as a friend there is no limit to how much she will meddle for them. The English instead makes the sentence about Haruki considering Io a friend, losing the general character rule that explains both her fury and why he can entrust Setsuna to her.
findings.japanese:
一部を除いて、友達と認めた相手には、
限りないお節介を焼く、俺の類友。
findings.todokanai: Apart from the other person present, namely Takeya, she's someone I consider a friend, one whose tendency to meddle with others' business seems to be almost limitless, much like mine.

findings.highlight: Io slapped me on my left cheek
findings.evidenceJa: 依緒の手が閃くのに合わせ、今度は左の頬を差し出した。
findings.explanation: As Io's hand flashes, Haruki deliberately offers his left cheek this time. The English reports only that Io slapped him, deleting his active acceptance of punishment immediately after admitting that another cherished feeling has taken root in him.
findings.japanese:
依緒の手が閃くのに合わせ、
今度は左の頬を差し出した。
findings.todokanai: In a flash, Io slapped me on my left cheek this time.

findings.highlight: not caring if even a single girl was watching us
findings.evidenceJa: 女の子が誰も見ていないにも関わらず、背中合わせで情けなカッコいい言葉を交わしていた。
findings.explanation: The joke is that Haruki and Takeya exchange pathetically cool, back-to-back lines despite there being no girls present to witness the performance. The English says they do not care whether girls are watching, replacing the absent-audience punchline with indifference to an audience.
findings.japanese:
なんて、俺たちは、
女の子が誰も見ていないにも関わらず、
背中合わせで情けなカッコいい言葉を交わしていた。
findings.todokanai: We had a cool albeit pathetic exchange as we sat back to back, not caring if even a single girl was watching us.

findings.evidenceJa: 二人して赤く染まった頬を押さえながら。
findings.explanation: Both men are holding their cheeks, reddened by the blows they have received. The English treats the red as blushing embarrassment and omits the held cheeks, severing the final physical payoff from the confrontation that produced it.
findings.japanese: …二人して赤く染まった頬を押さえながら。
findings.todokanai: …All the while trying to hide our embarrassment.
